items.title: Dave Rivello interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rochester, New York, January 11, 2012
items.q: The interviewee mentions 'Csus' only as a chord voicing ('harmony is just Csus') within an anecdote about a lesson with Bob Brookmeyer. There is no mention of a person named 'Csus'.

ctx.x: there’s all these scales. And if I look at a Dm7 chord, I think of it as a major scale with a lowered third and a lowered seventh. I don’t think Dorian. Why should I think Dorian?

I don’t think you need to. I think if thinking a lowered third and a lowered seventh works for you, and this is the way I teach, then that’s the way you should think of it. Somebody else may think oh it makes it so much easier for me to think Dorian, then that’s the way they should think about it and not as a major scale with a lowered third and a lowered seventh. But that’s where we were. And so the amount of information that is out there now is overwhelming. I even teach in my jazz pedagogy class at Eastman, I…

at least for me, maybe everybody else knows this I don’t know — but he said, “Books are just a summation of somebody else’s experience. Have your own experience.” And so my job is to do my work. And however I think about it, it doesn’t have to line up with anybody else’s way of thinking about it, it’s just that I have to go to work every day and if I reinvent the wheel that’s okay because it’s my wheel and I own that wheel now. So that’s the way I look at it. So hopefully that answers the question.
